description: The Office of Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) is seeking motivated college students, recent graduates, and graduate students for the Fall 2026 Internship Program in her Washington, D.C., office. Intern responsibilities vary daily but typically include assisting with constituent services, sorting mail, answering phones, conducting legislative research, attending hearings and briefings, and providing general administrative support to staff. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain firsthand experience in a congressional office, develop professional skills, and contribute to the work of Congresswoman Kaptur and her team.
responsibilities: Providing general administrative support to staff
qualifications: Strong written and oral communication skills
Interest in public service and the legislative process
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment
Organized, dependable, and eager to learn
Ties to Ohio are strongly preferred but not required
how_to_apply: Interested candidates should submit a single PDF containing a current résumé, a one-page cover letter outlining interest in the position and availability, and a short written response (300–500 words) to the prompt: What does public service mean to you? Send completed applications in a SINGLE PDF to angela.maloney@mail.house.gov with the subject line: Fall 2026 Internship Application – [Your Name]. Application Deadline: July 21, 2026, at noon.
equal_opportunity: The Office of Congresswoman Kaptur is an equal-opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status.

description: A senior Republican member serving on the House Financial Services Committee is seeking a fellow to assist the Legislative Team in covering the committee and research portfolio. This is a paid opportunity. The person in this role will work on substantive financial services issues like banking, crypto, housing, capital markets, fintech, insurance, and monetary policy in the Member's personal office. The fellow will also be asked to assist the Legislative Director in research projects. The fellow will also be attending hearings, monitoring legislation and regulations, assisting with official and constituent correspondence, providing meeting materials, and more. The fellow should leave this role with an in-depth understanding of how Capitol Hill operates, as well as the major policy issues in financial services.
responsibilities: Writing briefing materials for meetings with the Member
Preparing materials for hearings, markups, and the House floor
Taking notes at meetings, hearings, briefings, and other events you attend
Attending hearings, monitoring legislation and regulations
Assisting with official and constituent correspondence
Assisting the Legislative Director in research projects
qualifications: Able to work in a fast-paced environment
Background in finance, financial policy, and or Capitol Hill experience is not required but strongly preferred, whether it is in the private sector, government, or school
how_to_apply: Interested candidates should send their resume to Jackson.notes@mail.house.gov and joseph.arbie@mail.house.gov.

description: The Democratic Staff of the Committee on Rules is seeking part-time or full-time, energetic interns for the fall (September/October – mid-December). Interns work closely with Committee staff to prepare materials for Committee meetings, conduct research projects, learn about the Rules of the House and the various procedures for legislation to reach the House Floor, and complete a variety of other administrative tasks. Interns will gain experience in legislative analysis, political communications, and institutional processes. A stipend will be available for qualified candidates. Massachusetts ties are a plus. All offers are conditional on completion of a federal criminal background check.
responsibilities: Learn about the Rules of the House and the various procedures for legislation to reach the House Floor
Complete a variety of other administrative tasks
qualifications: Interest in learning about House floor procedures
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should submit a resume and cover letter explaining why you want to join the Democratic staff of the House Rules Committee to democratsrules.house.gov/about/internships. Please indicate your availability on a week-to-week basis (e.g. PT/FT) and your potential start and end dates. No calls or drop-ins, please. The deadline to apply is July 10, 2026.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds or with untraditional experience to apply.

description: Congresswoman Dina Titus (NV-01) seeks highly motivated Legislative Interns in her D.C. office for Fall 2026. Interns in our D.C. office will have the opportunity to witness the legislative process and the inner workings of Capitol Hill first-hand. The internship will run from August through December, from 9:00am—6:00pm when Congress is in session and from 9:00am—5:00pm when Congress is not in session. This is a full-time internship.
responsibilities: Providing tours of the United States Capitol
Conducting legislative research to support the needs of the Congresswoman's staff
qualifications: Excellent oral and written communication skills
Ties to Nevada's First District are a plus but not required
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should use the link below to fill out the form and include a cover letter, resume, and short (1-2 page) writing sample. Applications will be accepted until Friday, July 10, 2026, on a rolling basis.
equal_opportunity: The office of Congresswoman Dina Titus is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status.

description: The Office of U.S. Representative Mark Takano (CA-39) seeks legislative and communications interns to serve for the Fall of 2026 in the Representative's Washington, D.C. office. Interns will work with the D.C.-based staff performing legislative, communications, and administrative work. Tasks include answering phones, sorting and drafting responses to constituent correspondence, attending briefings and hearings, performing legislative research, drafting communications material, and supporting staff members on various projects. All interns will be paid a monthly stipend of $1500. The application period for Fall 2026 internships is now open and will grant offers on a rolling basis until August 1st.
responsibilities: Sorting and drafting responses to constituent correspondence
Supporting staff members on various projects
qualifications: Commitment to public service and progressive values
State and/or district ties to Riverside, CA are a plus
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should go to takano.house.gov/services/internships and follow all instructions in order to apply.
equal_opportunity: The Office of Representative Mark Takano is an equal opportunity employer.

description: The Office of U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) seeks highly motivated, organized, and dedicated interns to serve for the Fall of 2026 in the Representative's Washington, D.C. office. Interns will work primarily with D.C.-based staff performing legislative and administrative work. All interns will be paid a one-time stipend of $5,850 unless funded by an outside organization. The application period for Fall 2026 internships is now open and will close on June 30th at 11:59 PM ET.
responsibilities: Sorting and drafting responses to constituent correspondence
Supporting staff members on various projects
qualifications: Commitment to public service and progressive values
how_to_apply: E-mail a resume, cover letter, short writing sample, three references, and availability to Jayapal.DCInternships@mail.house.gov with the subject "First Name.Last Name Internship Application." Application period closes on June 30th at 11:59 PM ET.
equal_opportunity: We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, age, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability. Diverse applicants encouraged to apply.
